annotation.method: Codex read the complete 55-page local paper, surveyed every section, algorithm, labeled theorem, lemma, corollary, appendix result, discussion, conclusion, and reference, visually checked all selected source pages, searched all 24 frozen mounted object modules, and compiled private N/L proofs before accepting the targets.
annotation.reason: The project owner assigned the P16 source selection and benchmark annotation to Codex.

corpus_membership: This paper is part of the current corpus listed in metadata/manifest.json.
paper_version: published open-access journal version; IMA Journal of Numerical Analysis 46(4), 2026, printed pages 1939-1993

rejected_candidates.candidate: floating-point notation, gamma definition, condition numbers, singular values, and forward/backward error definitions in Section 2
rejected_candidates.reason: These are definitions or recalled standard tools. T1 instead formalizes the exact perturbation-to-residual implication that makes the displayed backward-error formula operational.
They are assumptions of the framework rather than proved conclusions.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Theorem 3.1 full MOD-GMRES attainable forward/backward error theorem
rejected_candidates.reason: It is the central unrestarted result, but a source-faithful finite formalization would require singular-value optimization, key-dimension existence, least-squares backward stability, and the complete Paige-et-al. residual argument absent from the frozen baseline. Lemma 4.2 preserves the paper's reusable exact residual-composition core without pretending those delegated ingredients are formalized.
Its modular coefficients depend on every operation model and on Theorem 3.1. The selected T2 isolates its exact one-step engine, and T3 captures the resulting mixed-precision restart convergence.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Theorems 5.1-5.3 for HH-GMRES, MGS-GMRES, and FGMRES
rejected_candidates.reason: These compatibility results depend substantially on external Householder/MGS/Paige analyses. They are less novel than the Section 6 applications and would duplicate the same final residual shape.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Theorems 6.1 and 6.2 for simpler GMRES and CGS2-GMRES
rejected_candidates.reason: Both are viable but require formal QR/Arnoldi/Gram-Schmidt algorithms and singular-value rank conditions. Theorem 6.3 exposes the paper's most portable new finite-restart statement and admits a clean exact strengthening.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Theorems A.1, B.1, C.1, C.3, Lemma C.2, and Corollary C.4
rejected_candidates.reason: The appendices contain important supporting results, but they would require full finite QR/CGS2 implementations or polar/singular-value infrastructure. They are subordinate to the selected main-text progression.

rejected_candidates.candidate: prospective discussions of deflated, randomized, and block GMRES and all literature comparisons
rejected_candidates.reason: These are research directions, comparisons, or engineering guidance rather than completed universally quantified results of this paper.

T1.decision: Use the exact perturbed-solve residual estimate behind the normwise backward-error formula on printed page 1942.

T2.decision: Use the backward-error half of Lemma 4.2, replacing the paper's first-order comparison by the exact finite recurrence implied by (4.1), (4.2), (4.14), and (4.18).

T3.decision: Use Theorem 6.3 and make 'contracts by Lambda until the attainable floors' exact after every finite number of consecutive restarts via a Lambda-power certificate.

selection_policy: Use results proved in this paper and exact consequences of their displayed hypotheses, not empirical or prospective discussions.
Expose the paper's Euclidean/Frobenius normwise structure with finite-dimensional paper-scoped definitions.
Replace first-order comparison notation by exact inequalities and make the finite restart count explicit.
Keep every public definition paper-scoped and free of NumStability imports.
Assign tiers only from the 24 modules in metadata/library_olean.json.
